questions.title: Laplace maximum likelihood
questions.text:
A sample $x_1,\dots,x_n$ is modelled as i.i.d. Laplace with location $\mu\in\mathbb R$ and scale $b>0$:
$$f(x\mid\mu,b)=\frac{1}{2b}\exp\!\Big(-\frac{|x-\mu|}{b}\Big).$$
Write `mle_laplace(x)`, which takes the data as a list or array and returns the list `[mu_hat, b_hat]` of maximum likelihood estimates. When $n$ is even, any $\mu$ between the two middle observations maximises the likelihood; return the midpoint of the two middle observations.
questions.docs:
**Maximum likelihood.** The log-likelihood is
$$\ell(\mu,b)=-n\log(2b)-\frac1b\sum_i|x_i-\mu| .$$
For fixed $b$ it is maximised by the $\mu$ that minimises $\sum_i|x_i-\mu|$, which is a sample median. Then maximise over $b$ by setting $\partial\ell/\partial b=0$ with $\mu=\hat\mu$.

```
mu_hat <- median of x           (midpoint of the two middle values if n is even)
b_hat  <- mean of |x_i - mu_hat|
return [mu_hat, b_hat]
```

def mle_laplace(x):
    """Maximum likelihood estimates (mu_hat, b_hat) for i.i.d. Laplace data with density
    f(x | mu, b) = exp(-|x - mu| / b) / (2 b). Return a list [mu_hat, b_hat]."""

questions.referenceSolution:
def mle_laplace(x):
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)
    mu = float(np.median(x))
    b = float(np.mean(np.abs(x - mu)))
    return [mu, b]
questions.oracleSolution:
def expected_value(x):
    # independent of np.median: the location MLE minimises sum |x_i - m|, and the minimum is attained at a data point
    x = [float(v) for v in x]
    best = min(x, key=lambda m: (sum(abs(v - m) for v in x), m))
    odd = len(x) % 2 == 1
    if not odd:
        # with an even n every value between the two middle points is a minimiser; take the midpoint, as the median does
        s = sorted(x)
        lo, hi = s[len(s) // 2 - 1], s[len(s) // 2]
        best = (lo + hi) / 2
    b = sum(abs(v - best) for v in x) / len(x)
    return [best, b]
